title: Implement throttle
description:
Implement `throttle(func, wait)`.

It returns a new function that calls `func` **at most once every `wait` milliseconds**. The first call runs `func` immediately. Calls made during the following `wait` milliseconds are ignored, not queued. Once `wait` milliseconds have passed since `func` last ran, the next call runs it immediately again.

When `func` runs, it receives the arguments and the `this` value of the call that triggered it. The throttled function itself returns `undefined`.

**Example:** with `wait = 100`, calls at 0, 40 and 99 ms run `func` once (at 0 ms); a call at 100 ms runs it again.

**Constraints:** `1 <= wait <= 10000`. Each throttled function keeps its own state.

### How the tests work

Each test is a short script that calls your function and returns what it observed. Time is virtual: `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearTimeout`, `Date.now()` and `performance.now()` all read a test clock, and time only passes when a test calls `await clock.tick(ms)`. A test may use `spy()`, which returns a function that records every call as `{ args, at }` in `spy.calls`.

exampleTestCases.explanation: Calls at 40 and 99 ms fall inside the window opened at 0 ms and are dropped; the call at 100 ms runs.
func runs on the first call, and dropped calls are never replayed later.
